title: Tomato Soup with Cheesy Garlic Toast

items: 1 tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
1 tsp sugar (to soften the tomatoes' acidity)
¼ cup fresh basil leaves, chopped (about 10 leaves)
4 thick slices (¾ inch) Italian bread or sourdough

steps: Melt the butter in the pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 6–8 min, stirring, until soft and golden at the edges. Add the garlic and stir 1 min, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes, broth, salt, pepper and sugar. Bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer uncovered 20 min, stirring now and then, until slightly thickened.

During the last 5 min of simmering, set an oven rack 6 inches below the broiler and heat the broiler on high. Mix the softened butter and garlic in a small bowl. Spread it on one side of each bread slice and set them butter side up on a rimmed sheet pan.
Broil 1–2 min, until the edges are golden. Top with the mozzarella and broil 1–3 min more, until bubbling and spotted brown. Watch closely; it burns fast. Cut each slice into 4 squares.

Turn off the heat under the soup. Blend until smooth with an immersion blender. With a countertop blender, fill it no more than halfway, take out the center cap, cover the hole with a folded towel and blend in batches.
Stir in the cream and basil and warm over low heat 2 min without boiling. Taste and add salt.
Ladle into bowls, sprinkle each with 1 Tbsp parmesan and serve with the toast squares.
tips: No fresh basil: add 1 tsp dried basil with the tomatoes instead.
Fire-roasted crushed tomatoes give the soup a smoky flavor.
storage: Soup keeps in the fridge 4 days and freezes up to 3 months. Reheat over medium-low heat, stirring, without boiling. The toast is best fresh; re-crisp leftovers at 375°F for 5 min.
